answer: A port authority can require each vessel to post a ferrous anchor deposit before entering the harbor: a small, refundable stake of real value that is forfeited on proven misbehavior. One operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake ships, because every identity must carry its own anchor. A single thread of reputation then links each vessel's past conduct to its deposit, so honest operators build trust while sybils bleed cost with each fake identity they create.
